next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: AI-StoryForge Story Export & Sharing — EPUB/PDF Generation and Public Share Links
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Build a complete story export and sharing system on top of the per-user storage foundation established in this mission. The mission should accomplish: (1) Export engine — generate well-formatted EPUB and PDF versions of completed projects using the stage log content, with cover page, chapter breaks inferred from the story structure, and StoryForge branding. Store exports alongside other project files in outputs/users/{user_id}/{project_id}/exports/. (2) Public share links — allow users to generate a time-limited, token-secured public URL for any completed project (e.g. /story/{share_token}) that renders a read-only story view without requiring login. Track share link views in the download_log table with is_public=True flag. (3) Share link management on the Document Library page — list active share links per project, show view counts, allow revocation. (4) Admin visibility — show public share link activity in the admin project detail audit log. (5) Email delivery — add a 'Email me this story' button that sends the EPUB as an attachment using the existing email infrastructure. All export operations should be async (background job) with progress tracking reusing the existing job_registry pattern. Success criteria: user can generate EPUB/PDF from Document Library, copy a public share link, and optionally email the story to themselves; admin can see share link activity in audit log; all existing 59+ tests continue passing.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The per-user storage, download logging, and Document Library established in this mission create the natural foundation for export and sharing. Users who can now see their files logically want to share them. EPUB/PDF export adds tangible value that differentiates StoryForge from a raw text generator. Public share links drive organic growth (users sharing with friends). This mission reuses the job_registry, download_log, email infrastructure, and Document Library UI already in place — maximizing leverage on existing investment while delivering a high-value user-facing feature.

final_report.summary: The AI-StoryForge User Profiles mission was completed across 2 cycles, transforming the platform from a shared-storage multi-user system into a fully personalized, per-user experience. Cycle 1 laid the complete backend and template foundation: per-user SQLite storage with directory isolation, profile management with display names and writing preferences, password change flow, per-project file storage under outputs/users/{user_id}/{project_id}/, download logging with counters, admin project detail view with stage logs and file browser, and a history page View Files modal. All 59 tests passed at end of Cycle 1. Cycle 2 focused on polish, E2E validation, integration completeness, and UX additions: a dedicated Document Library page (/documents) with per-project file accordions, bulk ZIP download, individual file downloads with type icons; admin audit log table on project detail pages with AJAX refresh endpoint; display_name propagated into admin users list, admin user_detail header, and admin project ownership info; graceful handling of legacy projects with missing or non-existent workspace_path; per-user directory creation at project creation time; new test file test_cycle2.py and updated security regression tests. The system was validated end-to-end with the server running, screenshots captured, and all UI elements confirmed to render with real data rather than placeholder dashes.
key_achievements: Per-user file storage isolation: all generated files land in outputs/users/{user_id}/{project_id}/ with automatic directory creation
Full profile page with display name, writing preferences (genre, style, tone), password change, stats (projects, words, downloads), and quick links
Display name shown in nav bar, admin users list, admin user detail header, and admin project ownership panel
Dedicated Document Library page (/documents) with expandable per-project file accordions, file type icons, sizes, dates, individual and bulk ZIP downloads
Admin project detail page with stage log table, file browser, download buttons, and scrollable download audit log with AJAX refresh
Download logging: every file download records timestamp, user identity, IP address, admin flag — fully auditable
Legacy project backward compatibility: projects without per-user workspace_path return empty file lists gracefully rather than 500 errors
Documents nav link added to both navigation bar and profile quick links section
Admin download-log JSON API endpoint for AJAX refresh without full page reload
All 59 original tests preserved passing; new tests added for document library and admin download log endpoints
challenges_overcome: Merging per-user path logic into existing workspace_path model without breaking legacy projects that predate the per-user storage scheme
Ensuring display_name propagates consistently across all admin views (list table, detail header, project ownership) from a single source of truth in the users table
Building the Document Library ZIP bundling without introducing server-side file accumulation — streaming in-memory ZIP using Python's zipfile module
Handling the case where workspace_path exists in the database but the directory has since been deleted on disk — returning empty list rather than propagating FileNotFoundError
Keeping admin audit log table performant by limiting displayed rows and providing AJAX pagination endpoint rather than loading all historical records inline
lessons_learned: Per-user storage isolation is most cleanly implemented at project creation time (mkdir with parents=True, exist_ok=True) rather than lazily at first write — prevents scattered path-creation logic
Display name should be stored once and joined via SQL in all admin queries rather than looked up per-row in Python — avoids N+1 query patterns
File listing endpoints benefit from a single utility function that accepts a base directory, validates existence, and returns a typed list — reused across routes, admin routes, and document library
Download logging is most useful when it records is_admin separately from user_id so audit queries can filter admin-initiated downloads from user-initiated ones
Accordion-style document library UX scales better than a flat list once users have many completed projects — grouping by project keeps the page scannable
AJAX refresh on audit log tables is preferable to auto-polling — reduces server load while still enabling operators to manually check for new activity
